lesson_basicsIsolatedHonour_explain: The Red Dragon connects to nothing else in your hand. Discarding it keeps every set and partial set, and leaves you ready: one tile from winning.
lesson_basicsTwoSidedWait_prompt: Your hand is ready: one tile from winning. Pick every tile that wins.
lesson_basicsTwoSidedWait_explain: 4-5 Characters is open at both ends: a 3 or a 6 completes the chow. That's twice the chances of an edge or closed wait, which only one tile completes.
lesson_basicsKeepTwoSided_prompt: Which discard leaves you waiting on the most tiles?
lesson_basicsKeepTwoSided_explain: Discarding the 5 Characters keeps 2-3, which waits on a 1 or a 4. Keeping 3-5 instead waits on the 4 alone.
lesson_basicsPairWait_title: Two pairs, two ways to win
lesson_basicsPairWait_prompt: Your hand is ready: one tile from winning. Pick every tile that wins.
lesson_basicsPairWait_explain: With two pairs, either one can become a pung while the other stays as the pair: an East Wind or a White Dragon wins.
lesson_basicsSimpleHand_prompt: You drew your winning tile. How many faan is the hand worth?
lesson_basicsSimpleHand_explain: All Sequences (1), Self-Draw (1) and Fully Concealed (1) make 3 faan, exactly the minimum to win. Your flower isn't your seat's flower, so it scores nothing, and holding it rules out No Flowers.
lesson_basicsDiscardWin_prompt: You can win on this discard. How many faan is the hand worth?
lesson_basicsDiscardWin_explain: Characters plus honors is a Half Flush (3), and the Green Dragon pung adds a Dragon Pung (1): 4 faan. A discard win gets no Self-Draw, and your exposed pung rules out Fully Concealed.
lesson_basicsAllCopiesVisible_prompt: East is close to winning. Which tile do you know is safe to discard?
lesson_basicsAllCopiesVisible_explain: Three West Winds are in the discards and you hold the fourth. Nobody else can hold one, so nobody can be waiting on it for a pair or pung, and with all four 9 Dots out nobody can be going for Thirteen Orphans either. The lone 6 Bamboo is one of the tiles East is waiting on.
lesson_basicsNoChance_prompt: East is close to winning. Which tile can no chow be waiting on?
lesson_basicsNoChance_explain: All four 2 Characters are visible. A chow with the 1 Characters must be 1-2-3, so no chow can be waiting on it. Only a single wait or a pair wait could still take it, which is rare.
lesson_basicsTutorial_welcome: Welcome to the table. You sit at the bottom as East, the dealer. Play goes counter-clockwise: you, then South on your right, West opposite and North on your left.
lesson_basicsTutorial_yourHand: These are your 13 tiles. A winning hand is four sets and a pair. A set is three in a row of one suit (a chow) or three of a kind (a pung).
lesson_basicsTutorial_draw: North discarded, so it's your turn: you drew a tile from the wall. You now hold 14, so discard one.
lesson_basicsTutorial_discardFirst: Discard the Green Dragon. It's on its own, and nothing in your hand can join it in a set.
lesson_basicsTutorial_pungOffer: South discarded an East Wind and you hold two. You can claim any player's discard to complete a pung (碰).
lesson_basicsTutorial_pungLaid: Your East pung is laid face up. East is both your seat wind and the prevailing wind, so it scores 2 faan. After a claim you discard without drawing.
lesson_basicsTutorial_chowOffer: North, on your left, discarded the 4 Characters, which makes a chow with your 3 and 5. You can chow (上) only the discard of the player on your left.
lesson_basicsTutorial_kongOffer: South discarded the 9 Dots and you hold three. Four of a kind is a kong (槓).
lesson_basicsTutorial_replacement: A kong uses four tiles but counts as one set, so you drew a replacement tile from the back of the wall.
lesson_basicsTutorial_discardAfterKong: Discard the White Dragon. That leaves you ready: a second 2 Dots wins.
lesson_basicsTutorial_selfDrawn: You drew the 2 Dots yourself, and your hand is complete. Winning on your own draw is a self-draw (自摸), and all three other players pay.
lesson_basicsTutorial_result: The hand scores 4 faan: Seat Wind 1 and Prevailing Wind 1 for the East pung, Self-Draw 1 and No Flowers 1. That clears the 3 faan minimum, so each player pays you.

lesson_minedEfficiency_prompt: Which discard keeps your hand closest to winning, with the most unseen tiles that help?

lesson_minedDefenceAllCopiesVisible_prom: An opponent is close to winning. From what you can see, which tile is certainly safe?
lesson_minedDefenceAllCopiesVisible_expl: {tiles}: every copy is visible, so nobody can hold one for a single wait or a pair wait, and no chow or Thirteen Orphans wait can still take it. Nobody can win on it.
lesson_minedDefenceNoChance_prompt: An opponent is close to winning. From what you can see, which tile can no chow be waiting on?
lesson_minedDefenceNoChance_explain: {tiles}: every chow through it needs a tile whose four copies are all visible, so no chow can be waiting on it. A single wait or a pair wait could still take it, so this is a strong read, not a guarantee.
